clue.text: Black Beauty, for instance an unexpectedly successful entry

parts.note: black means dark in colour
Black Beauty is the horse in Anna Sewell's novel, so Beauty is an example of a horse

explanation.surface: The famous fictional horse turns out to be a surprise winner in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The italicised title reads as one name, but it splits: Black gives the colour word and Beauty is an example of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an outsider who surprisingly wins a race or contest is called this.

clue.text: Very small device for tracking down internal strife

indicators.note: internal means the conflict word sits inside the device

parts.note: DF is a direction finder, used to track a signal
war is strife or conflict

explanation.surface: A tiny gadget used to hunt out conflict within an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a miniature version of something is described as this, as in a dwarf conifer.

clue.text: Soldier in uniform

definitions.meaning: a professional soldier in a standing army

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'uniform' is an adjective, not military dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: a career soldier, and an even, consistent pattern.

clue.text: Beautiful woman uplifted by injured hero -it comes out at Christmas

indicators.note: by here lets the scrambled hero take the turned word in among its letters
injured means the letters of hero are hurt into a new order
uplifted in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A lovely woman is lifted up by a wounded hero during the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: The turned beauty sits inside the scrambled hero; 'by' is a loose container signal. The Christmas rose is a winter-flowering plant of this genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Christmas rose, a hellebore, blooms around midwinter.

clue.text: High wind may make waves

parts.note: literally a gale tossing a vessel; figuratively causing trouble in a settled group

explanation.walkthrough: 'make waves' is the idiom for stirring up trouble, which the literal storm picture disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to upset a stable situation, just as a gale tosses a small vessel.

clue.text: You say it's a farm animal?

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the pronoun spoken aloud

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a certain creature belongs on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female sheep, kept on farms.

clue.text: Young man in charge of three dimensions

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, as in a cub reporter or young lad

explanation.surface: A junior employee is put in charge of a project spanning three dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a solid having length, breadth and depth is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Police hold up naked boy

indicators.note: hold means the police letters contain the next word

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
taken as written

explanation.surface: Officers stop an unclothed lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' reads as a robbery but splits: 'hold' is the container and 'up' its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Roman god of love is shown as a naked winged boy.

clue.text: Polish sailors I encountered in the outback

indicators.note: in places the sailors and I inside the outback word

parts.note: the bush is the Australian outback
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Polish seamen meet the narrator in the Australian wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality because it starts the clue; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rub to a shine.

clue.text: Manipulating deal, perhaps fish with those competing

parts.note: carp is a freshwater fish
an entry is the set of competitors in a race

explanation.surface: Fixing a business deal involving fish and rival bidders.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal here is pine or fir timber, not a transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: working timber such as deal is the woodworker's craft.

clue.text: Nice gal, relaxed and beautiful

indicators.note: relaxed suggests loosened up, so the letters of the two words are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasant young woman, calm and good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective (or the French city) but is anagram fodder with 'gal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone of heavenly loveliness, like a seraph, is described with this word.

clue.text: Roman Empire receded without a ruler.

annotationWithheld.why: Roman Empire receded without a ruler (7), answer EMPEROR: scan confirms the wording, but no parse of the remaining words builds the letters, and no source gives the setter's wordplay
annotationWithheld.clue: Roman Empire receded without a ruler.

clue.text: Forged note taken to school

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A counterfeit banknote is handed in at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a banknote beside 'Forged', but here it is the musical note of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a forged document is fake, not genuine.

clue.text: Try out stroke at end of match

indicators.note: at end of places the stroke word after the match word

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a drive is an attacking stroke in cricket or golf

explanation.surface: A batsman tries out a shot in the closing stages of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a cricket international match (a sport played chiefly in Britain and Commonwealth nations).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sample a car on the road before buying, or more generally to trial something.

clue.text: Crag above part of New York, a popular place with visitors

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the crag word before the next

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky crag
New York City is divided into five boroughs

explanation.surface: A cliff overlooks a New York district, which attracts tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARBOROUGH is a seaside resort town in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Yorkshire seaside resort is a holiday destination.

clue.text: Motor starts to clatter and rattle

indicators.note: starts to signals taking the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An old engine begins to clank and shake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: motor is a British word for an automobile.

clue.text: Bird deposits rubbish on island

indicators.note: on puts the rubbish word on top of the island word in a down clue

parts.note: chaff is husks, worthless stuff
an inch is a small island in Scottish place names

explanation.surface: A bird drops waste onto an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common European finch.

clue.text: Put one's hand out -— it's simple

definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: spread the fingers and then close them again
an idiom for a case or matter that is obvious and easily settled

explanation.walkthrough: The first half describes the physical action of unclenching and clenching a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an obvious, easily decided case is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Chips are difficult to take in — chap had to swallow one

parts.note: deep means hard to understand

indicators.note: to swallow means the name takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: Fred is a typical man's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man struggles to digest chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is a link word. 'Chips are' is a descriptive definition: the answer completes the sentence about chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: fried chips are cooked immersed in hot fat.

clue.text: Lute had to be replaced quickly

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A broken lute must be swapped for a new one in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had to be' looks like the verb but supplies letters to the anagram with 'Lute'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a military command meaning at running pace, hence very fast.

clue.text: Include at no extra cost a restart for game

definitions.meaning: add something free as part of a deal
in football, a way of restarting play after the ball crosses the touchline

explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: adding a free extra, and the football restart taken from the touchline.

clue.text: Travel regularly to work

definitions.meaning: a ferry or bus that goes back and forth along a route

explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: ships move regularly along a route, and one works at a trade, both expressed by this verb.

clue.text: Physiologist supported by a dancer

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue puts the second piece beneath the first

parts.note: Ivan Pavlov was the Russian physiologist famous for conditioning dogs

explanation.surface: A scientist is held up by a ballet performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna PAVLOVA was a celebrated Russian ballerina.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a famous Russian prima ballerina.

clue.text: Elemental spirit

parts.note: fire is one of the four classical elements
water is another of the four classical elements

explanation.surface: A ghostly being made of the natural elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elemental' gives two of the four classical elements side by side; 'spirit' means strong liquor, not a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a name for strong distilled liquor such as whisky or gin.

clue.text: Court extremely dingy, with lots of wainscotting

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of dingy

explanation.surface: A gloomy courtroom heavily panelled in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a room with much wooden panelling has plenty of timber.

clue.text: Father admits I have some money

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A priest confesses to having some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A FIVER is a five-pound note in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a five-pound note is a sum of money in British usage.

clue.text: In fashion, new stove

indicators.note: In places the letter inside the fashion word

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion

explanation.surface: A trendy new cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a range is a large kitchen cooker.

clue.text: In the middle of the day we returned to the top of Mornington Crescent

indicators.note: In places the reversed word and letter inside midday

parts.note: noon is midday

indicators.note: returned means the word we is turned round
the top of picks the first letter of Mornington

explanation.surface: Travellers come back at lunchtime to a London Underground station.
explanation.walkthrough: Mornington Crescent is a London Underground station, but 'Crescent' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the moon in its early phase shows as a thin crescent.

clue.text: Careless mistake member of teaching staff picked up

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A lecturer's slip is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests noticing; it turns the word upwards. Even Homer nods: a lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a lapse of attention, as in Homer nodding.

clue.text: Fabulous creature -one some might say I feed

parts.note: 'un is the dialect form of one, as in a good 'un
corn is animal feed

explanation.surface: Someone claims they feed a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some might say' marks a dialect form, not a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a horse-like mythical beast with one horn is a creature of fable.

clue.text: Thank you for tucking away the tissue

indicators.note: tucking away means the run of letters is concealed inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A grateful note for keeping a tissue safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small handkerchief, or a paper tissue used like one.

clue.text: Heated, dry out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Warmed up, a thing dries out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: heating something dries it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to remove water from something, as heating does.
